questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests precise bit-mmask construction under edge-case shifts; no loops/branches is a common constraint in low-level systems.

## Key Concepts
- Bit masks and ranges
- Safe shifts with variable width (1..32)
- No branching; single expression mask composition

## Code Example
```javascript
uint32_t clearRange32(uint32_t x, unsigned a, unsigned b) {
  unsigned w = b - a + 1; // width of range
  uint32_t ones = (~0u) >> (32 - w); // w ones in LSBs
  uint32_t mask = ~(ones << a); // zeros in [a,b], ones elsewhere
  return x & mask;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to generalize to 64-bit with the same constraints?
- What if inputs are signed; does behavior change in C/C++?

## Why This Is Asked

Assesses ability to manipulate a 128-bit value using two 64-bit parts and leverage available intrinsics for performance. It tests understanding of bit significance ordering and boundary cases (zero input).

## Key Concepts

- 128-bit represented as two 64-bit words (lo then hi) and how trailing zeros map across the boundary

- Correct handling of the all-zero input returning 128

## Code Example

```c
int trailingZeroCount128(uint128 x) {
  if (x.lo != 0) return __builtin_ctzll(x.lo);
  if (x.hi != 0) return 64 + __builtin_ctzll(x.hi);
  return 128;
}
```
